Hi Oliver,

Quick technical note from Identity: when Redwood's Coupa connector attempts to auto-map a vendor to a tenant we rely on one of two signals in the SAML assertion: a verified email domain or an explicit organization attribute (we expect attribute name 'organization' or 'org' depending on the IdP schema). We've run into cases where the vendor IdP sends the company under a different attribute (e.g., 'orgName' or 'company_display') and our mapping rule doesn't pick it up, which results in an invite that lands but isn't associated with your tenant.

What we need from your IdP admin (two options):
- Add or map an assertion attribute named 'organization' (case-insensitive) containing exactly the legal entity string you want linked to the tenant (example: 'Greensmith Logistics LLC').
- Or ensure your email domain (the part after @) is included as a verified domain in your Coupa account; if your corporate emails are @greensmith.com that will generally work.

If neither is possible quickly, I can issue a manual invite and perform a tenant override on our end (temporary). I have opened support ticket SUP-78431 to track this and included internal mapping notes here: https://docs.redwood.com/internal/sso/tenant-mapping.

I'll attach a small sample mapping snippet for your IdP admin to copy (plain text). Once the attribute is present, try re-accepting the invitation.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Identity Engineer, Redwood Inference
